Subject: Quick confirm — demo at KubeCon tomorrow (10:00)

Alex —

Looking forward to the on-site walkthrough tomorrow at KubeCon. I sent a calendar invite for 10:00; I intended that as 10:00 Europe/Madrid local time (CET).

Attendees from our side: me, Marissa (solutions), and Tessa (field). Can you confirm the room where you'd like us to meet (hotel lobby, booth D, or a private room)? A lot of the conference spaces are doing last-minute room shuffles and I want to avoid a repeat of the usual clock mix-ups.

I'll attach the latest deck and an updated .ics pinned to Europe/Madrid timezone in my next email. If you prefer, we can also switch to a video link at the same local time.

— Karthik

Cc: ops@starlight.ai
Subject: Re: Quick confirm — demo at KubeCon tomorrow (10:00)

Karthik —

Thanks for the note. Heads-up: I showed up at the hotel lobby at 09:00 this morning (based on the invite on my phone) and the space was empty. The concierge said their wall clock was still on summer time and an hour behind the conference rooms. It turned into a bit of a scramble for us.

Looking at the invite in my calendar it showed 10:00 but didn’t label the zone clearly, and my phone defaulted to PST for some reason (I was triaging travel). I realize this is partly on me, but given the number of attendees who are traveling, can we use explicit timezone labels (e.g., "10:00 Europe/Madrid (CET)") in the subject or body and pin the invite to that zone?

Also: can we confirm whether the booth demo is still planned for 14:00 local at Hall B (I was told two different times by the organizer). If we can lock the runbook and send a single calendar update with the ICS that forces Europe/Madrid, that would help.

Appreciate it — I don't want our execs waiting around again.

— Alex
Alex Wong
Head of Platform, Starlight AI
alex.wong@starlight.ai

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Subject: Re: Quick confirm — demo at KubeCon tomorrow (10:00) — updated invite attached

Alex — really sorry about the confusion and thanks for flagging. That must have been frustrating. We're tracking two causes here: (1) some hotel clocks on the property were still on DST, and (2) my original invite didn't force the Europe/Madrid timezone on the .ics (I created it from a laptop set to PDT, dumb mistake).

Action items done now:
- I attached an updated-invite.ics that is explicitly set to Europe/Madrid (CET). Please accept that one — it should override local calendar defaults.
- Updated the event subject to read: "Redwood demo — 14:00 Europe/Madrid (CET) — Hall B, Booth 9" so the local time is obvious in the subject line.
- Added the booth contact and a one-line runbook in the calendar description so the concierge can direct you.
- Attached the slide deck again for quick reference.

If you'd rather move to a private room earlier in the day (13:00 Europe/Madrid) to avoid the expo noise, Marissa and Tessa are available. Suggested final slots: 13:00 (private room) or 14:00 (booth). Which do you prefer?

Again, apologies for the wasted time this morning — we'll make sure the team is waiting in the agreed location.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: updated-invite.ics (iCal), redwood-demo-deck.pdf (PDF)

Karthik —

Thanks for the fast update. We've accepted the new invite and the subject-line timezone callout is perfect. We'll plan to meet at 13:00 Europe/Madrid in the private room (Room P2, Level 1) — the ops team confirmed they can free the room for us then.

I'll forward this thread to our executive assistant so they see the pinned invite. For future on-site demos, could we add one line in the subject with the timezone (as you did) and add a short "If you're local, use hotel clock; if traveling, rely on event timezone: Europe/Madrid" note in the body? That has already saved us one awkward scramble.

See you at 13:00.

— Alex
